fi-pseudanthias-dispar.title: Dispar Anthias
fi-pseudanthias-dispar.summary: A peaceful Pacific anthias; males show a bright red dorsal fin. Best kept as one male with several females in a roomy reef.
rows: About 4 in; wild record 9.5 cm (3.7 in) TL (FishBase)
One male with a harem of females. A group needs about 125 gal; one fish alone can live in 70 gal
Carnivore (plankton picker). Frozen mysis and enriched brine shrimp in several small feedings a day; many later accept quality flake
Pacific Ocean: Christmas Island in the eastern Indian Ocean to the Line Islands, north to the Yaeyama Islands, south to the Great Barrier Reef, Fiji and Samoa
notes: Like all anthias it is a sex-changer: if the male dies, the top female can turn male.
In the wild it gathers in large schools along current-swept reef edges.

fi-pseudanthias-squamipinnis.title: Lyretail Anthias
fi-pseudanthias-squamipinnis.summary: An active, social anthias that helps bring shy fish out. Males are red; the females, like these SKUs, are more orange.
rows: About 5 in; wild record 15 cm (5.9 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep in a group with only one male. A species group needs 125 gal or more
Carnivore (zooplankton feeder). Frozen mysis and enriched brine shrimp several times a day; later small amounts of flake
Indo-West Pacific: Red Sea and Natal, South Africa to Niue, north to Japan, south to Australia
notes: The largest female changes into a male if the male is lost.
Mostly swims in open midwater but wants some hiding spots.

fi-pseudanthias-pleurotaenia.title: Squareback Anthias
fi-pseudanthias-pleurotaenia.summary: Also called the Squarespot Anthias. Females are yellow with a lavender belly; males are pink with a pale square patch on the side.
rows: About 7¾ in; wild record 20 cm (7.9 in) TL (FishBase)
One fish needs about 100 gal; a group needs about 180 gal
Carnivore. Frozen mysis and enriched brine shrimp in small, frequent feedings
Pacific Ocean: Indonesia to Samoa, north to Ryukyu Islands, south to New Caledonia and the Rowley Shoals in the eastern Indian Ocean and Christmas Island
notes: Colors hold best under dim, indirect light.
A deeper-reef species that hovers over steep drop-offs in the wild.

fi-pseudanthias-kashiwae.title: Red Fairy Anthias
fi-pseudanthias-kashiwae.summary: One of the easier anthias to keep. This SKU is a male.
rows: About 6 in; wild record 14 cm (5.5 in) TL (FishBase)
A group needs about 125 gal and lots of swimming room; separate fish if fighting turns serious
Carnivore (planktivore). Frozen mysis and enriched brine shrimp in small, frequent feedings; later quality flake
Indo-Pacific: East Africa to Samoa and the Line Islands, north to southern Japan, south to the Great Barrier Reef
notes: A refugium growing copepods and amphipods gives it steady live food.

fi-pseudanthias-randalli.title: Randall's Anthias
fi-pseudanthias-randalli.summary: A small, colorful anthias from deeper Western Pacific reef walls. Males show bright red, magenta and yellow striping; females are paler with a yellow snout. All start out female, and the dominant fish turns male.
rows: About 3 in (Saltwaterfish.com adult size); wild record 9.5 cm (3.7 in) TL (FishBase)
Keep one male with a few females, or a mated pair; never two males
Carnivore/planktivore: several small meals a day of copepods, frozen mysis, enriched brine shrimp and quality flake
Pacific Ocean: Philippines to Niue, north to the Ryukyu Islands
notes: Hardy for an anthias; give live rock with caves and hiding spots.
